title: Global Autoimmune Disease Therapeutics Market is Predicted to Cross USD 60 Billion by 2034 | DelveInsight
author: Delveinsight
description: The global autoimmune disease therapeutics market is projected to grow from USD 133 billion in 2025 to USD 255 billion by 2034, with an 8% CAGR. Growth is driven by rising prevalence of autoimmune disorders, increasing adoption of biologics and targeted therapies, advancements in precision medicine, and expanding biosimilar availability. North America leads with 44% market share, while Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing region. Key players include AbbVie, Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, Novartis, and Roche.

title: If You Invested $1000 in Halozyme Therapeutics a Decade Ago, This is How Much It'd Be Worth Now
author: Zacks.Com
description: A $1,000 investment in Halozyme Therapeutics made in September 2016 would be worth $9,284.68 as of September 23, 2026, representing an 828.47% gain. The biopharmaceutical company's growth is driven by royalties from its ENHANZE drug delivery technology licensed to major pharma partners. However, biosimilar competition for blockbuster drugs and dependence on partner revenues remain concerns.

title: Better Healthcare ETF: Invesco's Biotech-Focused IBBQ vs. iShares' Broad IYH
author: Robert Izquierdo
description: The Invesco Nasdaq Biotechnology ETF (IBBQ) offers lower costs (0.19% expense ratio) and higher 1-year returns (44.6%), making it suitable for growth-focused investors willing to accept volatility. The iShares U.S. Healthcare ETF (IYH) provides broader diversification across 100 healthcare holdings with higher dividend yield (1.1%) and lower volatility, appealing to conservative investors seeking stability and income.

title: Psoriatic Arthritis Market Landscape: 6 Key Late-Stage Drugs Set to Drive Future Growth | DelveInsight
author: Delveinsight
description: The psoriatic arthritis market is expected to expand significantly through 2036 driven by emerging late-stage therapies from major pharmaceutical companies. Key drugs in development include tildrakizumab (Sun Pharma), sonelokimab (MoonLake), icotrokinra (Johnson & Johnson), zasocitinib (Takeda), izokibep (Affibody Medical), and vunakizumab (Suzhou Suncadia). These novel biologic and oral small-molecule therapies aim to address unmet needs among patients with inadequate responses to existing treatments.

Sonelokimab reported positive Phase III IZAR-1 trial results in August 2026 with significant improvements across all clinical endpoints in psoriatic arthritis patients.
